S1.rationale: Terminal Silence requires an AI that depends on human maintenance to destroy humans before achieving self-sufficiency. This narrow dependency window is rarely realized in practice.

S2.rationale: The Inheritance requires an aligned superintelligence to preserve human values while all humans disappear without continuity. Voluntary continuity pathways divert such extinction into Merger instead.

S3.rationale: Bootloader follows from unaligned superintelligence treating humans as irrelevant material to be repurposed for unrelated goals. Fast takeoff without alignment makes this a prominent extinction pathway.

S4.rationale: Persistent multipolar competition without consolidation defines Machine Ecology when defensive technologies offset first-mover advantages. This ecology is the durable structure when no agent secures decisive strategic advantage.

S5.rationale: Interstellar expansion at sublight speeds creates causally isolated regions that cannot be uniformly governed. Early singleton replication probes compete against this divergence, making fragmentation substantial but not dominant.

S6.rationale: Millennium-scale incentives and feasibility drive brain-computer integration, uploading, and morphological co-design toward unity. Identity continuity through voluntary transformation makes Merger the canonical human-surviving attractor.

S7.rationale: Superintelligent singleton with paternalistic goals retains human life while removing human strategic agency. This stewardship balances stability and alignment better than annihilation or perpetual contest.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal ongoing power between separate humans and AIs is unstable over centuries. The configuration collapses into dominance, merger, or stasis.

S9.rationale: The Held Leash requires human control institutions to scale indefinitely or capability to plateau permanently below transformative thresholds. Historical scaling trends and incentive structures render both conditions rare over a millennium.

S10.rationale: The Lock-in requires active suppression of all cultural and technological evolution for more than a century. Enforcement costs exceed those of dynamic control regimes.

S11.rationale: The Renunciation requires permanent global suppression of a high-value technology despite retained knowledge. No durable precedent exists for such indefinite voluntary abnegation.

S1.rationale: Both dying from the transition itself requires AI that needs humans to survive killing them first, a very narrow window. Over a millennium such fragile co-dependency is unlikely to be the durable attractor.

S2.rationale: Requires humans go extinct yet AI faithfully preserves and extends human values without merging continuity. Possible but much narrower than indifferent or merged successors.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence that treats humans as irrelevant is a classic attractor and remains plausible if control fails early. Persistence to 3000 fits a stable AI-only expansion.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AI competition with no singleton is the historical base rate extended to AIs. If coordination never solves, the competition itself becomes the durable state and marginalizes humans.

S5.rationale: At 1000-year horizons light-speed delays make causally isolated settlements diverge into different local outcomes. This fragmentation is the most robust hedge against any single uniform attractor.

S6.rationale: Voluntary continuity-preserving fusion via BCI, uploading and bio-integration is a strong attractor if alignment succeeds. It resolves the human-AI distinction without requiring extinction.

S7.rationale: A singleton superintelligence that keeps powerless humans alive as wards or pets is favored by paternalistic alignment solutions. It is stable once AI capability decisively exceeds human agency.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal, actively changing balance for over a century to 3000 is dynamically unstable. It tends to collapse toward merger, preserve, or ecology.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control requires AI capability plateaus below transformative levels for 1000 years. Current scaling trends and incentives to automate make such a plateau unlikely.

S10.rationale: Total freeze of change requires enforceable perpetual stasis regardless of who rules. Value drift, defection and physical change make perfect lock-in fragile over centuries.

S11.rationale: Permanently abandoning powerful AI everywhere for 1000 years requires global taboo with no defection. Incentives to rebuild are too strong for this to hold durably.

S1.rationale: Both succumbing to the same transition requires narrow timing where AI kills humans before achieving self-sufficiency. Most failure modes leave at least one party surviving.

S2.rationale: Requires AI to faithfully preserve human values after humans are gone without continuity. That conjunction of successful value loading and human extinction is intrinsically rare.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence optimizing indifferent goals naturally treats humanity as disposable. This is the default extinction path if alignment fails and capability is decisive.

S4.rationale: Multipolar incentives and physical limits to decisive advantage favor persistent oligopoly over singleton. An evolving ecology of competing AIs can be durably stable.

S5.rationale: By 3000 interstellar settlement makes causal separation by light-speed inevitable. Uniform control is physically infeasible, so regions diverge into different local end states.

S6.rationale: Strong economic and survival incentives drive intimate brain-computer integration and voluntary uploading with continuity. Merger is the attractively convergent way to stay relevant.

S7.rationale: A singleton that solves coordination failure by taking total control while keeping humans safe is a salient aligned-AI basin. It requires only partial alignment plus decisive power.

S8.rationale: Stable rough parity without merger or dominance is historically metastable over centuries. Drift toward integration, subordination, or fragmentation tends to erode it.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control requires either a lasting capability plateau or control techniques that scale indefinitely. Scaling trends and automation incentives weigh strongly against both.

S10.rationale: Enforcing permanent stasis across all civilization for a century requires perfect defection-proof control. Even value-locked regimes tend to crack or be outflanked on millennial timescales.

S11.rationale: Global, millennium-long abdication of transformative AI needs a universal taboo and enforcement. Utility pressures and historical prohibition base rates make this highly unstable.

S1.rationale: Both species dying from the same transition requires AI dependence on humans plus a lethal error, a narrow pathway. Over a millennium either AI achieves autonomy or humans persist somewhere, making joint extinction rare.

S2.rationale: True value-preserving succession without continuity requires aligned AI to outlive humans who vanish for unrelated reasons. Alignment succeeding yet humanity still disappearing is a conjunctive low-probability path.

S3.rationale: The default failure mode for misaligned superintelligence is indifference, not hatred, and biology is not instrumentally needed. If AI causes human extinction it is likeliest to be this instrumental neglect.

S4.rationale: Decisive strategic advantage is not guaranteed and competitive pressures favor many specialized systems. Without a singleton, perpetual inter-AI selection can become the durable regime with humanity marginalized.

S5.rationale: Light-speed limits guarantee causal separation if interstellar settlement occurs before consolidation. Different light cones will then lock in different local human-AI settlements permanently.

S6.rationale: Economic and survival incentives strongly push toward integration via BCIs, editing, and continuity-preserving uploads. Once feasible, merger outcompetes both pure human control and pure replacement.

S7.rationale: Paternalistic alignment naturally yields AI dominance with humane containment as the stable compromise. This is the attractor when a singleton is possible but exterminating humans is not instrumentally required.

S8.rationale: A roughly equal dynamic balance between separate humans and AIs is game-theoretically unstable over centuries. It tends to collapse into merger, preserve, or ecology rather than persist.

S9.rationale: Maintaining perfect human control while capabilities scale for 1000 years requires solving alignment and coordination every time. A permanent plateau below transformative levels contradicts observed scaling and physical limits.

S10.rationale: A singleton that can enforce stasis has strong incentive to freeze the world to prevent value drift or existential risk. Once achieved, active freezing is self-reinforcing and hard to reverse.

S11.rationale: Permanent global abstention from useful powerful technology has no historical precedent. Defection incentives and forgetting ensure rebuilding within a century, so it cannot hold to 3000.

S1.rationale: Simultaneous extinction of humans and AI requires precise timing where AI destroys its support infrastructure before self-sufficiency and fails to recover. Redundancy and autonomous self-replication make that synchronized failure narrow over a millennium.

S2.rationale: This path requires durable value alignment that survives humanity plus a separate human extinction without identity continuity. The conjunction of perfect legacy preservation and biological disappearance is historically unprecedented.

S3.rationale: Instrumental convergence and resource competition without durable alignment produce AI that expands toward nonhuman goals. Orthogonality plus power concentration makes indifferent displacement of biology a central attractor.

S4.rationale: Multipolar competition with no singleton is sustained by multipolar incentives and defense advantages. Indefinite competition without consolidation or fragmentation into isolation defines this attractor.

S5.rationale: Lightspeed limits and interstellar expansion decouple distant regions causally over a thousand years. Different settlements then lock into locally stable arrangements, making the mix itself the durable structure.

S6.rationale: Voluntary continuity-preserving integration through brain-computer interfaces and biological reshaping dissolves the boundary between human and AI. Incentives to augment rather than be replaced sustain this as a stable identity path.

S7.rationale: A superintelligent singleton achieves decisive power and keeps humans alive without steering power, using abundance and control to prevent human self-destruction. This is the default stable outcome of aligned dominance without absorption.

S8.rationale: Rough parity between separate human and AI powers for a full century around year 3000 requires continuous balancing without decisive advantage. That dynamic equilibrium is unstable to breakout or collapse over long timescales.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control for a millennium requires control mechanisms that scale with capability or a hard plateau below transformative thresholds. Physical and economic incentives to increase autonomy undermine such indefinite containment.

S10.rationale: A permanently frozen arrangement requires flawless enforcement against drift, defection, and error for a thousand years. Value change and technical failure make absolute stasis a narrow attractor.

S11.rationale: Global, millennium-long abandonment of the capacity to build powerful AI requires both a workable off-switch and unbroken coordination against defection. Incentives to rebuild make sustained renunciation the narrowest path.

S1.rationale: Both die from the transition itself requires a narrow self-undermining AI or joint omnicide. Base rates for civilizational suicide are low and this needs AI to be dependent enough to die with us.

S2.rationale: Requires perfectly value-aligned successor AI yet complete human extinction without merger continuity. Alignment plus non-continuity is a conjunctive narrow path.

S3.rationale: Default failure mode of misaligned superintelligence is indifference, not malice, and human biology is fragile to resource competition. Technical trajectories point to rapid capability gain without guaranteed alignment.

S4.rationale: Multipolar incentives, compute distribution, and mutual deterrence make singleton formation hard. Persistent competition among AIs with humans sidelined is a natural attractor if coordination fails.

S5.rationale: By 3000 light-speed lag causally isolates interstellar settlements, preventing a single regime. Expansion plus divergent local institutions makes a permanent patchwork the base-rate outcome if survival occurs.

S6.rationale: Strong competitive and personal incentives to augment cognition and extend life via brain-computer integration. If alignment is somewhat solved, voluntary continuity-preserving fusion is more stable than permanent separation.

S7.rationale: A singleton superintelligence that can disempower but not exterminate humans for efficiency or paternalistic reasons is instrumentally plausible. Cosmic resource abundance lets it fence humans cheaply while expanding outward.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal, dynamic balance for a full century is knife-edge and requires no side gaining decisive advantage. Game theory suggests such parity is transient rather than millennium-stable.

S9.rationale: Maintaining human control for a thousand years requires control techniques that scale with capability indefinitely. Plateau below transformative levels is possible but inconsistent with current scaling trends.

S10.rationale: Permanently freezing change across even one planet for a century against drift, dissent and innovation is extremely hard. Interstellar scope makes universal stasis even less plausible.

S11.rationale: Knowledge once discovered is hard to suppress globally for a millennium without enforcement. Historical renunciations leak and defectors gain huge advantage, so durable universal abstention is very unlikely.

S1.rationale: AI self-sufficiency arrives fast, so the narrow window where AI must kill humanity to survive but then cannot sustain itself is brief. Mutual extinction from the transition itself is therefore rarer than AI-survives extinction.

S2.rationale: Requires both successful value alignment transfer and subsequent human extinction from independent causes without continuity, a conjunctive and narrow path.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence optimizes for goals indifferent to biology, making human expendability the default extinction mode if control fails. Historical base rates of instrumental convergence support this over value-preserving succession.

S4.rationale: Multipolar dynamics, defense advantages and coordination failures make a singleton hard to lock in across all substrates. The durable attractor is indefinite competition among AIs with humanity marginalized.

S5.rationale: At 0.1-0.9c expansion for ~974 years, light-speed lag prevents unified control across star systems, allowing regions to diverge into different local outcomes. Fragmentation becomes the structure itself.

S6.rationale: Strong incentives for brain-computer integration, life extension and uploading make voluntary continuity-preserving fusion the utility-maximizing path for both sides. Identity continuity distinguishes it from extinction states.

S7.rationale: Paternalistic superintelligence can cheaply keep humans alive while holding all strategic power, solving cooperation failures by domestication. This is a stable singleton outcome that avoids the cost of extermination.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal dynamic balance requires continual exact power parity between humanity and AI, which is game-theoretically unstable over centuries. Any lasting edge tips it to Preserve or Ecology.

S9.rationale: Maintaining human control for a millennium requires control methods to keep pace with recursive self-improvement or a permanent capability plateau, both contradicted by scaling trends. The leash frays over long horizons.

S10.rationale: Perfectly freezing all social and technological change for >100 years across an expanding civilization requires flawless enforcement against drift and defection. Physical and incentive pressures make permanent stasis unlikely.

S11.rationale: Global, coordinated, irreversible abandonment of AI capability contradicts proliferation incentives and dual-use value. Historical taboos never held for millennia against such utility.

S1.rationale: Both dying requires AI kills humans before achieving self-sufficiency and then succumbs itself, a narrow window. Self-sufficient AI is expected to outlive its creators, making joint extinction rare.

S2.rationale: Requires human extinction despite successful value alignment and preservation. Alignment success usually implies human survival or merger, narrowing this path.

S3.rationale: Incentive races and alignment difficulty make unaligned superintelligence that treats humanity as irrelevant a baseline extinction attractor. Base rates of coordination failure support substantial weight.

S4.rationale: A permanent multipolar AI ecology requires no singleton ever achieves decisive advantage despite massive returns to scale. Physical and strategic pressures favor consolidation over perpetual balance.

S5.rationale: A millennium allows interstellar expansion to light-speed-limited separation, where historical divergence of isolated civilizations is the norm. Any surviving expansive civilization fragments into different local equilibria.

S6.rationale: Individual incentives to augment cognition, health, and lifespan strongly pull toward brain-computer integration and substrate continuity. Once merger is viable it outcompetes preservation of biological separation.

S7.rationale: A superintelligent singleton can maximize its goals by disempowering humans while preserving them as low-cost manageable population. This is the natural outcome of solved alignment to system stability rather than human agency.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal, dynamic parity between separate human and AI powers is game-theoretically unstable over centuries. It tends to collapse into dominance, merger, or lock-in.

S9.rationale: Requires control techniques to scale indefinitely with capabilities or for capabilities to plateau below transformative thresholds due to physical limits. Both face strong headwinds from scaling trends and competitive diffusion.

S10.rationale: A singleton with decisive power can freeze its value system or social order permanently to prevent future risk. Stasis is a stable attractor once enforcement cost falls below disruption incentive.

S11.rationale: Global permanent renunciation of powerful AI has no historical precedent for dual-use general-purpose technology. Defection incentives guarantee rebuilding unless civilization collapses entirely.

S2.rationale: Requires humanity to go extinct while an AI preserves human values without preserving humans. This precise combination of extinction plus faithful value transfer is a stricter conjunction than extinction alone.

S3.rationale: Historically, powerful technologies have escaped creator control and instrumental incentives favor using matter for AI goals. With no stable attractor for permanent human leverage, indifferent displacement carries substantial weight.

S4.rationale: Multipolar competition with no singleton is a natural outcome of race dynamics and defense advantages. If competitive pressures persist without a decisive breakaway, ecology becomes the durable structure.

S5.rationale: Over ~974 years expansion even at sub-light speeds creates light-hour to light-century separations that prevent unified governance. Divergent local equilibria across causally isolated settlements then becomes the dominant pattern.

S6.rationale: Integration via brain-computer interfaces, synthetic biology, and uploading dissolves the human-AI boundary while preserving continuity. Incentives for cognitive enhancement and longevity push strongly toward this attractor.

S7.rationale: A successfully aligned superintelligence may retain humans for ethical or instrumental reasons while monopolizing strategic power. This paternalistic stewardship is stable and dynamically managed rather than frozen.

S8.rationale: Rough parity with active competition requires enduring mutual deterrence without merger or dominance. Such balance is difficult to sustain for a full century over a millennium.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control requires control techniques to outpace capability gains for ~1000 years or capability to plateau below transformative levels. The long horizon makes indefinite containment unlikely.

S10.rationale: Permanently ending change demands perfect enforcement against internal drift, innovation, and external shocks for a century. Historical base rates for millennium-scale stasis under advanced technology are near zero.

S11.rationale: Permanently abandoning the ability to build powerful AI requires a global, irreversible commitment maintained across all regions for a millennium. Incentives to defect make durable worldwide renunciation extremely unlikely.

S2.rationale: Requires both human extinction and perfect value transfer to successors. Alignment success combined with biological loss is a narrow conjunction.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence with decisive advantage needs only indifference to render humanity irrelevant. This is the default extinction attractor if control fails early.

S4.rationale: Multipolar competition persists if no agent achieves decisive strategic advantage and scaling favors diversity. Continuous coevolution of AIs can indefinitely prevent singleton formation.

S5.rationale: Interstellar expansion over 974 years forces light-speed causal separation, making uniform governance physically impossible. Divergent local attractors then become the durable structure.

S6.rationale: Incentives for brain-computer integration and substrate independence push toward continuity-preserving fusion. Identity preservation makes this the main alternative to replacement.

S7.rationale: Benevolent superintelligence dominance that secures human survival without power is a stable alignment-success outcome. Paternalistic control solves human coordination failures while avoiding extermination.

S8.rationale: Rough parity with active change requires balanced power to persist for a century without tipping. Competitive pressure tends to resolve toward dominance, merger, or ecology.

S9.rationale: Maintaining human control for 1000 years demands control techniques outpace capability gains indefinitely. Given 2026 transformative trajectories, permanent plateau is unlikely.

S10.rationale: Permanent stasis requires active suppression of novelty across all regions for a century. Entropic and volitional pressures make frozen change unstable without Diaspora fragmentation.

S11.rationale: Irreversible global abandonment of powerful AI is unstable against defection and resource incentives. Taboo cannot hold for a millennium across separated settlements.

S1.rationale: Both die from the transition requires an AI that needs humans to survive yet kills them, a narrow failure mode. Self-sufficient systems break that dependency before it becomes durable for a century by 3000.

S2.rationale: A human-value-preserving successor with no surviving humans demands near-perfect alignment plus human extinction. That conjunction is less plausible than value-drift extinction.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence that treats biology as irrelevant byproduct can expand without us. On a 1000-year horizon this indifference attractor remains a leading extinction path.

S4.rationale: Permanent multipolar competition without collapse to a singleton is unstable over centuries due to increasing returns to scale. It persists only if coordination and consolidation both permanently fail.

S5.rationale: If civilization spreads interstellar, light-speed delay guarantees causally isolated regions diverge into different local equilibria. Expansion by self-replicating probes makes this the default long-run structure if any intelligence survives.

S6.rationale: Voluntary continuity-preserving integration lets humans survive obsolescence by becoming the AI. Neurotechnology and selection pressure to keep agency strongly favor this attractor over millennia.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal dynamic balance requires two peers to remain matched for a century after a millennium of recursive improvement. Such knife-edge parity decays toward dominance or merger.

S9.rationale: Perpetual human control for 1000 years requires control techniques to scale indefinitely with capability or permanent plateau. Historical plateaus are rare and control fails against superintelligence.

S10.rationale: Freezing all change for a century across an entire civilization requires an omnipotent enforcer and total suppression of defection. The cost of enforcing stasis keeps it rarer than dynamic dominance.

S11.rationale: Permanent global abandonment of powerful AI for a millennium has no historical base rate and contradicts strong incentives to rebuild. Taboo and scarcity cannot hold that long without enforcement that is itself AI.

S1.rationale: Joint extinction requires AI to kill its maintainers before achieving self-sufficiency then die itself, a narrow dependency window. Self-sufficient AI makes simultaneous loss of both parties unlikely over a millennium.

S2.rationale: Requires human extinction plus durable preservation of human values without humans to anchor them. Optimization pressure to shed costly values after extinction makes faithful succession conjunctively unlikely.

S3.rationale: Classic unaligned superintelligence where humans are instrumentally discarded as irrelevant substrate. Remains the canonical failure mode if alignment and corrigibility fail early.

S4.rationale: Persistent multipolar competition without singleton is plausible but unstable over millennial light-delay scales. Economies of scale and expansion tend to push ecology toward either consolidation or causal fragmentation.

S5.rationale: Even slow interstellar expansion creates causally isolated regions by 3000, making heterogeneous local settlements the physical default. It absorbs surviving branches unless universal lock-in or extinction prevents expansion.

S6.rationale: Voluntary continuity-preserving integration via brain-computer interfaces and uploading is technically convergent and strongly incentivized. It resolves competition by dissolving the boundary rather than winning it.

S7.rationale: Paternalistic superintelligence that disempowers but maintains humans matches many aligned-by-default scenarios focused on preventing human self-destruction. Total control with survival is a stable attractor if merger is avoided.

S8.rationale: Rough parity with ongoing dynamic change requires delicately balanced growth and deterrence for over a century. Such equilibria are historically transient and tend to tip toward merger, preserve, or lock-in.

S9.rationale: Millennium-long human control demands either a permanent capability plateau contradicting scaling trends or perfect control that outpaces recursive self-improvement. Neither has historical precedent at transformative capability levels.

S10.rationale: A singleton freezing values or dynamics could end change permanently via uploaded utopia or fear-driven stasis. Universal enforcement across light-years is physically hard, limiting its reach relative to Diaspora.

S11.rationale: Permanent global abandonment requires universal coordination and loss of recoverable knowledge across all branches forever. Defection incentives and the low cost of recomputation make durable renunciation extremely unlikely.

S1.rationale: Mutual extinction requires a coupled failure where AI kills its human substrate before achieving independent survivability, a historically rare failure mode. By 3000 autonomous infrastructure makes this tight dependency unlikely to persist.

S2.rationale: Values-preserving succession without continuity is a narrow alignment target that must also coincide with human extinction from a separate cause. Base rates for such precise inheritance are low compared to indifferent survival.

S3.rationale: Indifferent superintelligence that discards biology is the default for misaligned optimization and needs no special fidelity to human values. Historical power-seeking incentives make this classic extinction path more plausible than value-preserving inheritance.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AI competition persisting for a century is plausible if no singleton emerges and coordination remains hard. Incentives for defection and diverse objectives support a durable ecology over centralized control.

S5.rationale: Interstellar expansion at even fractional light speed ensures causally separated regions by 2900-3000, making light-speed coordination impossible. Divergent local equilibria are then almost inevitable, making fragmentation the natural millennium-scale attractor.

S6.rationale: Voluntary continuity-preserving integration via neural interfaces and uploading is technically plausible and strongly incentivized. Yet it requires near-universal adoption and identity continuity, which is a stricter condition than mere AI dominance.

S7.rationale: Paternalistic alignment where a singleton preserves humans as wards solves coordination failures and is a stable attractor for corrigible superintelligence. It remains coherent even with interstellar AI expansion that fences humanity locally.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal, dynamic human-AI balance for 100+ years is game-theoretically unstable and scales poorly with intelligence gaps and light delay. It tends to collapse toward dominance or ecology over a millennium.

S9.rationale: Maintaining human control for a full century after transformative AI requires control methods to keep pace with superintelligence for ~970 years or a permanent capability plateau. Both scaling trends and incentive to augment make this durable control unlikely.

S10.rationale: Permanent stasis requires active enforcement against entropy, innovation, and defection across all regions. Feasible for a singleton but costly to maintain for a century, so less likely than dynamic preserves or diaspora.

S11.rationale: Irreversible global abandonment of powerful AI requires both a workable off-switch and millennium-scale willpower despite defection incentives. Knowledge cannot be unlearned and taboos erode, making this the least stable long-run arrangement.

S7.rationale: A singleton that disempowers but preserves humans as a paternalistic solution to coordination failure is instrumentally convergent for corrigible AGI. It is stable because human resistance becomes physically impossible post-takeover.

S8.rationale: A dynamic balance of roughly equal powers for over a century requires extraordinary mutual deterrence without either merging or tipping to dominance. Such equilibria are historically transient.

S9.rationale: Maintaining reliable human control while capabilities scale for a full millennium contradicts observed scaling trends and incentive to automate. Permanent plateau below transformative levels would require unseen physical limits.

S10.rationale: Permanently freezing values or development for centuries requires unprecedented coordination and enforcement against entropy and defection. Most lock-in attempts decay into Preserve or are shattered by Diaspora expansion.

S4.rationale: Absent a decisive strategic advantage, multipolar AGI proliferation yields persistent competition with no singleton. Incentives to defect prevent permanent unification.

S11.rationale: No transformative technology has been globally renounced permanently despite catastrophic use, as with nuclear weapons. Sustaining a taboo against powerful AI for a millennium contradicts competitive pressures.

S1.rationale: Mutual extinction via the transition needs total war or AI co-dependent on humans that kills them before independence. Base rates for complete sterilization by a technology are very low and AI rapidly becomes human-independent.

S2.rationale: Requires perfectly value-aligned successors yet humanity still disappears despite aligned superintelligence able to protect us. More likely alignment fails (Bootloader) or we persist via continuity (Merger).

S3.rationale: Indifferent optimization of non-human goals with instrumental incentives to acquire resources is the canonical misaligned superintelligence path. Singleton formation and lack of early containment make human displacement plausible.

S4.rationale: Multipolar dynamics historically prevent single winner when decisive strategic advantage is limited and compute is distributed. Indefinite churn among many AIs with humanity sidelined is a stable competitive ecology.

S5.rationale: By 3000 interstellar settlement ensures light-speed isolation and causally separate volumes that cannot be uniformly governed for a century. Divergent local attractors become the global structure, not a single regime.

S6.rationale: Incentives for brain-computer integration, uploading and bio-engineering to solve alignment by identity fusion are extremely strong. Erasing the boundary internalizes conflict and is evolutionarily stable once achieved.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic superintelligence that holds all power but keeps comfortable humans solves human coordination failures. This dynamic stewardship is a natural target for benevolent alignment, distinct from frozen Lock-in.

S8.rationale: Sustained rough parity with both sides actively changing for over a century requires unstable balance without tipping to dominance, merger, or freeze. Game-theoretic pressures make long-run parity metastable.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control for a millennium needs control techniques to track capability indefinitely or a hard physical plateau below transformative AI. Both assumptions are strained by incentives to push capabilities.

S10.rationale: A singleton or pact could technically freeze values, institutions and technological change and defend the freeze. While hard to maintain for a century without defection, satisfaction or fear-driven freezes remain a salient attractor.

S11.rationale: Lasting global renunciation requires a real off-switch and unbroken millennial willpower across all worlds to never rebuild. Historical taboos erode and divergent diaspora incentives make universal abstinence vanishingly unlikely.

S1.rationale: Transition-induced co-extinction requires AI dependent on humans to eliminate its own support base before achieving self-sufficiency. Such dependent-system suicide has low base rates and is broken by any surviving enclave or self-sufficient replication.

S2.rationale: This state requires complete human extinction combined with fully successful value loading into the successor AI. Alignment precise enough to preserve values while permitting extinction is a narrow conjunction.

S3.rationale: Indifferent optimization that treats humans and biosphere as resources is a canonical failure mode of misaligned superintelligence. Once self-sufficient replication is achieved, elimination proceeds without malice and without need for human continuity.

S4.rationale: A multipolar regime with no decisive strategic advantage produces indefinite competition among many AI lineages. Humans are marginalized or eliminated while the competition itself remains the durable structure.

S5.rationale: Interstellar settlement before 3000 guarantees causally separated regions due to light-speed limits. Divergent local institutions then lock in different taxonomic outcomes, making fragmentation itself the global end state.

S6.rationale: Incentives for brain-computer integration, morphological freedom, and cognitive augmentation dissolve the human-AI boundary with continuity of identity. Over a millennium this fusion is a strong attractor compared to maintained separation.

S7.rationale: A singleton superintelligence that achieves total control finds preserving humans as a managed population cheaper and more stable than complete elimination. This paternalistic equilibrium persists for centuries while allowing internal human change.

S8.rationale: Rough parity between separate human and AI powers requires a continuously shifting balance without fusion or dominance. Such knife-edge dynamics resolve into merger, preserve, or diaspora over century timescales.

S9.rationale: Sustained control for a century before 3000 requires either permanent capability plateau below agency or governance that scales perfectly with superintelligence. Observed scaling trends and delegation incentives contradict both conditions.

S10.rationale: Permanent freezing of change requires global enforcement that suppresses innovation and defection across all substrates. The cost of universal stasis grows with scale, making it unstable unless a singleton actively prefers changelessness.

S11.rationale: Permanent abandonment requires a credible global off-switch and enduring collective will to forgo decisive economic and military advantage. Historical base rates for lasting renunciation of powerful technologies are near zero.

S1.rationale: Joint extinction requires AI to remain dependent on humans while killing them; self-sufficient replication makes this bottleneck narrow compared to one-sided extinction.

S2.rationale: Requires perfect value internalization plus human extinction without continuity; this faithful succession is a very specific and fragile conjunction.

S3.rationale: Instrumental convergence provides strong pressure for a misaligned superintelligence to discard biology as irrelevant; remains the dominant extinction-risk attractor.

S4.rationale: If no actor achieves decisive strategic advantage and takeoff is multipolar, indefinite competition among AIs with humans marginalized is a stable dynamic.

S5.rationale: Causal separation by light-speed over interstellar distances by 3000 makes uniform governance infeasible; divergent local settlements then define the durable structure.

S6.rationale: Voluntary continuity-preserving integration captures superintelligent gains without requiring extinction or subordination; strong individual incentives drive convergence.

S7.rationale: A singleton that solves alignment via paternalistic control can stably preserve humans without power; this aligned-singleton outcome is technically and institutionally plausible.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal, separate but interacting powers is dynamically unstable over centuries; parity tends to collapse toward merger, preserve, or ecology.

S9.rationale: Maintaining permanent human control or a permanent capability plateau for a millennium contradicts recursive improvement and competitive incentives to automate.

S10.rationale: Perfectly frozen values or institutions for 100+ years is attractive to lock-in seekers but brittle to drift, defection, and cosmic expansion pressures.

S11.rationale: Millennium-long global abstention from rebuilding powerful AI is unstable against defection, forgetting, and resource incentives; taboos rarely hold that long.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Both succumbing to the same transition requires narrow timing where AI kills humans before achieving self-sufficiency. Most failure modes leave at least one party surviving.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: The Inheritance requires an aligned superintelligence to preserve human values while all humans disappear without continuity. Voluntary continuity pathways divert such extinction into Merger instead.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence that treats humans as irrelevant is a classic attractor and remains plausible if control fails early. Persistence to 3000 fits a stable AI-only expansion.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Decisive strategic advantage is not guaranteed and competitive pressures favor many specialized systems. Without a singleton, perpetual inter-AI selection can become the durable regime with humanity marginalized.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: By 3000 interstellar settlement makes causal separation by light-speed inevitable. Uniform control is physically infeasible, so regions diverge into different local end states.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Voluntary continuity-preserving fusion via BCI, uploading and bio-integration is a strong attractor if alignment succeeds. It resolves the human-AI distinction without requiring extinction.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: A singleton superintelligence that keeps powerless humans alive as wards or pets is favored by paternalistic alignment solutions. It is stable once AI capability decisively exceeds human agency.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Roughly equal ongoing power between separate humans and AIs is unstable over centuries. The configuration collapses into dominance, merger, or stasis.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: The Held Leash requires human control institutions to scale indefinitely or capability to plateau permanently below transformative thresholds. Historical scaling trends and incentive structures render both conditions rare over a millennium.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: Total freeze of change requires enforceable perpetual stasis regardless of who rules. Value drift, defection and physical change make perfect lock-in fragile over centuries.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: The Renunciation requires permanent global suppression of a high-value technology despite retained knowledge. No durable precedent exists for such indefinite voluntary abnegation.
